explanation: The dot product measures how much two vectors point the same way. Numerically it is ax·bx + ay·by, and geometrically it equals |a||b|cos(theta), so its sign tells you the angle: positive means an acute angle, zero means perpendicular, negative means obtuse. The purple bar shows the projection of b onto a (its length is a·b divided by |a|) — rotate b with the angle slider and watch the dot product swing through zero exactly when b is perpendicular to a.
bullets: a·b = ax·bx + ay·by, and equally |a||b|cos(theta) — two views of the same number.
Sign tells the geometry: + acute, 0 perpendicular, − obtuse.
a·b equals |a| times the signed projection of b onto a (the purple bar).
